section_summary: This section (pages 51-81) documents SCAP and State Department activities regarding intellectual property in occupied Japan during 1948-1949, centering on the competitive bidding program for Japanese publishers to acquire translation rights to foreign books. It covers administrative licensing of French copyright representation, despatches forwarding the second and third lists of offered foreign titles, press releases, bidding results, and a Soviet protest over excluded works. In addition, the section addresses Far Eastern Commission deliberations on copyright and trade-mark restoration, alongside correspondence regarding Warren Jefferson Davis's prewar copyright infringement claim against Japan.

subfiles.about: Grants a commercial license to the Republic of France to assign translation rights of French copyrighted books to Japanese publishers.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: Authorizes France to sell translation rights of French books to Japanese publishers under strict currency and occupation regulations.
subfiles.title: GHQ SCAP Memorandum: License to Engage in Business in Japan (FI-97)

subfiles.about: Transmits the second list of foreign copyrighted books offered to Japanese publishers and an accompanying press release.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch forwarding the second list of 81 foreign books offered for Japanese translation rights.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 661: Second Offering of Foreign Copyrighted Books

subfiles.about: Presents 82 foreign titles made available for competitive translation and publication bidding in Japan.
subfiles.from: Civil Information and Education Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Lists 82 foreign titles across science, social studies, and literature available for Japanese translation bidding.
subfiles.title: Second List of Books Offered to Japanese Publishers for Competitive Bidding

subfiles.about: Announces 82 foreign books offered for translation, alongside news on SCAP libraries, weather, and war crimes trials.
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Press release announcing 82 foreign books for translation, including reports on SCAP information libraries and war crimes trials.
subfiles.title: Press Release: More Foreign Books Offered to Japanese Publishers

subfiles.about: Reports bidding results for the second foreign book offering and transmits the third offering list.
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports 38 Japanese publishers won rights to 58 titles and forwards a third list of foreign titles.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 698: Further Foreign Copyrighted Books for Translation and Publication in Japan

subfiles.about: Enumerates 52 foreign titles open for translation bids from Japanese publishers.
subfiles.from: Civil Information and Education Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Lists 52 foreign titles, primarily American scientific and technical works, offered for translation bidding.
subfiles.title: Third List of Foreign Books Offered to Japanese Publishers for Competitive Bids

subfiles.about: Announces the availability of the third list of 52 foreign books for Japanese translation.
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, GHQ Far East Command
subfiles.summary: Announces the release of a third list of 52 foreign books offered for competitive bidding.
subfiles.title: Press Release: Announce Third List of Foreign Books for Translation

subfiles.about: Reports on Japanese publishers acquiring translation rights to 58 foreign books approved by SCAP.
subfiles.from: Nippon Times
subfiles.summary: News clipping detailing successful bids and royalties paid by Japanese publishers for 58 foreign titles.
subfiles.title: Newspaper Article: 40 Publishers Bid on Foreign Books

subfiles.about: Transmits successful bids for the third book offering and reports a Soviet protest regarding rejected titles.
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports successful bids for 39 third-offering titles and discusses a Soviet protest concerning excluded books.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 783: Publication Rights of Foreign Copyrighted Books Acquired by Japanese Publishers

subfiles.about: Specifies winning publishers, royalty rates, print runs, and prices for 39 foreign titles.
subfiles.from: Civil Information and Education Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Tabulates 39 successful Japanese bids for foreign books, listing winning publishers, royalty rates, print quantities, and prices.
subfiles.title: List: Successful Bidders for Translation Rights of Foreign Books

subfiles.about: Recommends sending a draft cable to SCAP regarding Far Eastern Commission policy on copyright restoration.
subfiles.from: Noel Hemmendinger, Assistant Chief, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs
subfiles.summary: Recommends transmitting a cable querying SCAP's views on re-establishing copyright protection and FEC policy.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Copyrights
subfiles.to: Max W. Bishop, Chief, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs

subfiles.about: Inquires about SCAP plans for reopening the Copyright Office and re-establishing foreign copyright protections.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Requests SCAP's views regarding the reopening of Japan's Copyright Office and FEC copyright restoration policy.
subfiles.title: Draft Cable to SCAP: Reestablishment of Copyright Protection in Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Queries SCAP regarding renewal of pre-war American trade-marks, marked as withdrawn.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Draft inquiry on prewar American trade-mark renewals in Japan, noted as withdrawn by phone on March 31.
subfiles.title: Draft Cable to SCAP: Renewal of American Trade-Marks in Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Records the charge-out of file 894.54211/3-1546 concerning Marks & Clerk.

subfiles.summary: Standard form recording loan of file 894.54211/3-1546 to T. Maurer on January 31, 1952.
subfiles.title: Charge-Out Form DS-933a: File 894.54211/3-1546

subfiles.about: Records the charge-out of file 894.544/1-1348 concerning W. Jefferson Davis.
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records (RM/R)
subfiles.summary: Standard form recording loan of file 894.544/1-1348 on April 18, 1952.
subfiles.title: Charge-Out Form DS-933a: File 894.544/1-1348

subfiles.about: Advises that war claims against Japan await congressional legislation or a peace treaty.
subfiles.from: Benedict M. English, Assistant Legal Adviser, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Informs Davis that copyright infringement claims against Japan depend on congressional war claims legislation or a peace treaty.
subfiles.title: Letter from Benedict M. English to Warren Jefferson Davis

subfiles.about: Inquires about procedures for his copyright infringement claim regarding his book on Japanese air menace.
subfiles.from: Warren Jefferson Davis
subfiles.summary: Presses for procedures to settle his claim against Japan for unauthorized prewar publication of his book.
subfiles.title: Letter from Warren Jefferson Davis to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Records the charge-out of file 894.544/11-448 regarding W. Jefferson Davis.
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records (RM/R)
subfiles.summary: Standard form recording loan of file 894.544/11-448 on April 14, 1952.
subfiles.title: Charge-Out Form DS-933a: File 894.544/11-448

subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum regarding the War Claims Act of 1948.
subfiles.from: Benedict M. English, Assistant Legal Adviser, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Encloses State Department memorandum on the War Claims Act of 1948 regarding Davis's copyright infringement claim.
subfiles.title: Letter from Benedict M. English to Warren Jefferson Davis

subfiles.about: Inquires which State Department branch handles citizen claims and queries impounding of Japanese credits.
subfiles.from: Warren Jefferson Davis
subfiles.summary: Requests information on which office handles claims against Japan and whether Japanese credits are being impounded.
subfiles.title: Letter from Warren Jefferson Davis to Secretary of State
